answer: Use a lagoon escrow market: each agent locks stake in a lagoon pool, and peers bet stakes on whether it will misbehave. Raters vouching for fraudsters lose stake, so fake reputation gets quadratically pricier per vote. Each identity grows its own willow branch of sequential proofs; one stream cannot water two branches, so clones each pay full price. When a branch is caught, its willow cluster is slashed from the lagoon by the square of its size, like a dune caving in. Splitting into n identities multiplies stake at risk by n squared, not n, since escrow cannot be shared across clones.
